Title: Contesting a Vampire - an alternate mechanic.

Messages.Author: Wilsoros
Messages.Body:
Hello folks,

There have been a lot of post on this topic, and I have a new idea for
the rule, it is very much outside of the current mechanics, but I
thought it may be an interesting idea for discussion.

Contestation:
During your untap phase if a vampire you are contesting a vampire with
another methuselah you may choose to relinquish the contestation and
turn this vampire into an investment (or similar key word) with
counters equal to the blood on the vampire. As a master phase action
you may take two pool from this investment (or similar key word) to
your pool, burn this card when the last counter is removed. On the
turn you relinquish contestation and turn this vampire into an
investment, you gain 4 additional transfers.

The reason I like this mechanic is it gives you an option to stop the
damage but not be destroyed. If you play a mono-crypt deck, I am
sorry that is a risk and I am not sure this rule helps you at all.

A concern I have is if you have a 3 cap contested you gain 4
transfers, so perhaps it needs a minimum capacity requirement.

I would love to read constructive criticisms,

All the best
David Wilson
Ann Arbor

Messages.Author: Mark
Messages.Body:


Although I do like a fresh perspective in the whole discussion, I
think your idea still doesn't make it less 'harsh' if one of your
vampires gets contested.

You already address the fact that the four extra transfers can be an
advantage if a low cap vampire gets contested. If you take that
advantage away by using a minimal cap requirement for this 'rule' to
be in order, you also create a 'punishment' for using low caps instead
of high caps, since the latter will get the extra transfers.

The second thing I tend to dislike in this idea is the fact that it
will cost you a master phase action to transfer back pool. I remember
when our group first started playing; Short Term Investments were
really popular for pool gain! That was before we got to grips with the
rules, and finally understood that cards like Minion Tap were NOT bad
because they emptied your vampires of all that precious blood. The
point that I want to make here is that there is a reason why you see
those investment cards so little; master phase actions tend to be too
valuable!

So even though the idea would provide a way of getting your pool back,
it seems to me that contesting a vampire is punished too harsh. Which
I think is what started the discussion in the first place...

I'm not wild about the master phase action requirement. Although,
clearly, any possibility at getting pool back is better than none, quite
a few decks are already making a lot of use of master phase actions.
Having to choose between them? Not so fun.

It also still leaves you in a position where (for example) you bring out
a 10 cap, get it contested, and drop to 11 pool as you bring out a 9 cap
with no vampires - perfectly ordinary in some fatty-driven deck types
that use, for example, Parity Shift and Deflection to offset this.

>A concern I have is if you have a 3 cap contested you gain 4
>transfers, so perhaps it needs a minimum capacity requirement.

Actually, I'd not be so bothered by that. If someone brought out the 3
cap and contested it with you, they know they're potentially giving you
4 extra transfers. If you bring it out to contest someone else's, they
can do that themselves and thwart you getting the extra transfers anyway
(because you regain control of your 3 cap after they've yielded).

Also, just generally, a rule doing with a corner case like this would
(IMO) benefit from being brief and simple. Rules invoked only rarely
are better being short, sharp and straightforward. Example: the
Paralyze rules of old were a pain in the arse, so were dropped.

Messages.Author: Mathieu Rivero
Messages.Body:
I gave an alternate mechanic yesterday on the huge whine thread. Let
me copy/paste that and a small bit of chat that occurred later.

Now, it's true that contesting most of the time ruins two players,
especially on high capacity vampires. I'd like to make a suggestion to
LSJ : let's not change contesting rules, but add a new influence
rule.

"During your influence phase, spend 4 transfers to move all blood on a
contested minion to one of your uncontrolled vampire or imbued. Remove
the contested minion from the game. (The other contested minion is
turned face up as usual, at his controller's untap phase.)"

This allows several game mechanics about contesting :

> contesting is still bad. If no one yields, pool keeps to be lost. (outcome : keeps game diversity)
> contesting slows contested vampires but does not kill the yielding methuselah. (outcome : contesting is bad, but not deadly)
> contesting can be a strategy (If A plays Stanislava, that she is downed to a few bloods, then B contests Stanislava. A will ponder "do I yield now or lose transfers to gain some pool?")

A few cases to illustrate what this suggestion can lead to :
-A plays stanislava, B stops influencing her, then plays another
vampire. B is slowed, A plays with stanislava, her blood drops down,
then B contests : the benefit of having played with a contested
vampire will be balanced by the fact the vampire has less blood.
-A and B play stanislava. A uses the new influence rule, but just has
Nadima and another stanislava to influence on to. If he keeps
buggering B he will contest stanislava again. If he's smart and if he
wants to play, he will play Nadima and loose 3 blood in the process,
plus the 1 pool burned to keep contesting. So, as I said, contesting
is still bad with this rule.

Then, a guy said :
> We still have the issue with contestation, but it is still not clear
> to me (and many others it seems) why you feel that you cannot address
> the old issue with a different approach, without also removing/
> changing the old proposed solution. Unless it is because you feel the
> game game mechanic wise must remain at some status quo, and that
> leaving this untouched would greatly inbalance the game? I sincerely
> doubt that will be the case.

My concern was diffrent from what you think : it's not particularly
that "the actual game mechanic is wise", but more "if we dramatically
change the system, many errata and general game balance will have to
be made". It's true that if you play a mono-deck (like, turbo cybele
CotGB, or the polemic turbo Ian Forestal :p) and you are contested,
it's still a serious issue. However, if you do not have a plan B, it's
because you chose that weakness. Since you, as both player and
deckbuilder haven't thought about a backplan, you've got to pay the
price of that decision. And anyway, any deck will have a blindspot.
This solution takes just a line or two in the rulebook, and does not
affect general gameplay since vampire contesting is a cornercase.

One more thing : library cards contesting is a more frequent issue and
the harsh old way of dealing with it works fine, if you ask me, and I
doubt many players find it unbalanced. I think it's better to have a
general rule for contests and then an additional option to give a
lifesaver to vampire/imbued contesters.

If we keep the solution I proposed (thanks for the compliment
mate ;) ), the main concern I have is about "coming into controlled
region effects" (like Tariq, Anarch Convert, and so on and so forth.)
The fact is, a lot of rulings already exist, and just need to be
checked out and updated, and I don't think many of them will need
changes.

That's all I have to add on this, but i'd like to add a word on the
previous alternative way. If you spend a master phase action to gain
two pool, you lose all the defence you can get from a Pentex
Subversion or a Direct intervention ! Hope that helps :)

Revision:

another methuselah you may choose to relinquish the contestation and

you may take two counters off this card, burn this card when the last

It removed the master phase action requirement, although sill limits

Messages.Author: Wilsoros
Messages.Body:
I am excited that this issue is getting so much attention, so I want
to try to break down the problem a little to make sure we all agree to
what it is, and how severe.

When you suffer contestation:
(1) You lose several turns of transfers if playing with a large
vampire, which is normally at a disadvantage give 5 two caps will
often overwhelm a 10 cap.

(2) You lose all the pool.

(3) You are unable to build up your offenses and defenses due to the
above.

I am sure the three points can be rephrased better and I encourage
other to do it, I will try to edit this thread to reflect the changes.

Mathieu suggested spending 4 transfers to move the counters off the
afflicted vampire and onto a new one in your uncontrolled region.
This addresses (1) and (2) and only slows you down an additional turn
for (3), which can be quite daunting, although if your predator
contested you then she is likely down as well.

I suggested gaining 4 extra transfers by relinquishing the vampire,
than gaining 2 of the pool every turn during some phase of play. My
idea addresses (2) although slowly, it also partially addresses (1) by
giving 4 extra transfers, and in the same way as Mathieu somewhat
mitigates (3) although slower than Mathieu does.

This post doesn't add any new ideas, but I think it parses them into
points of discussion, I welcome your feedback,

All the best,
David Wilson
Ann Arbor

Messages.Author: Mathieu Rivero
Messages.Body:
This is sad, because so many good ideas spring from this few posts...

Wilsoros, there is something that bothers me in your solution :

If you relinquish a contest with your way, you already are in a bad
situation, for you're defenceless. The huge whine about Ian Forestal
leaves me completely indifferent, but I always found unjust that
contesting would make you loose with a 99% chance if you yield, and
that the turns you can't play are totally wasted. If we want to deal
with that particular issue the change must be immediate.
The four extra transfers you suggest seem a bit out of range : You
play Arika, then your Arika is contested. Bad. Then you've got no
vampires. If you immediately relinquish, you can start influencing 8
on Marcus Vitel. Except that your pool is 30-11-8-Masters-bleeds =
relatively few, at most 11, given your predator isn't aggressive,
which is rarely the case - anyway, if he/she sees you're contesting,
he will try to oust you the faster he can. Sure you'll gain 2 pool
turn by turn, but this pool gap isn't good, because this is the main
issue with contesting crypt cards (also given mono-vampire decks
contesting does not get my attention.)
Your solution was elegant, but there's a gap to fill. And also,
contesting and/or relinquishing wouldn't have been a tactic. So I
still prefer my solution. :)

And, I maintain that contesting has to remain a danger to prevent mono-
decks or unoriginal decks. :)

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
On Aug 23, 6:42 am, Mathieu Rivero <riveromath...@googlemail.com>
wrote:

> And, I maintain that contesting has to remain a danger to prevent mono-
> decks or unoriginal decks. :)

Except that:

A) Mono vampire/Superstar decks aren't good enough to need this brutal
of a safety valve (i.e. your game is simply over if you randomly sit
at a table where someone else wants to use the same guy), especially
as mono vampire/superstar decks are easily foiled by other, incredibly
common and mundane aspects of the game (Pentex Subversion, kill the
superstar, block fails tech, intercept as the superstar is tooling up,
not drawing the superstar in the first place, etc.)

B) It has been clearly shown that fear of contestation in no way
dissuades "unoriginal" decks. If you go look at the TWDA, for example,
the most common vampires occurring are exactly the ones that you would
expect (Arika, Anson, etc.)

So while I can certainly see opposition to changing the penalties for
contestation based on just not wanting to change the rules, or being
totally ok with the random harsh hosing factor of it, I can't in a
million years see "Don't change the contestation rules as superstar
decks need the punishment and it makes people not use the obvious
powerful vampires" as a remotely viable argument.

-Peter

> illustrating (well, not that Arika would show up even more if not for

I don't really agree that it can be said to do a poor job without
having any information about how the TWDA would look without "fear of
contestation", but I see your point.

without it Arika would possibly show up 100 times more than now. And
since that information isn't shown in the TWDA, the conclusion that
"fear of contesting" doesn't do anything can't really be drawn from
looking at the TWDA.
That's my whole point.

if
that's what you read in my post."

But then later you adjusted. Which is fine. But you certainly were
accusing me of doing so at some point. But we can move on.

> Sure, the "fear of contestation" isn't a 100% certain way to prevent
> certain vampires from being used more often than others. I've never
> said that though.

I didn't say that you did. But someone did. The argument of "the harsh
rules for contestation make people not use the popular/powerful
vampires" comes up all the time. And did in this very thread (which is
why I responded in the first place). And all indications are that this
is not actually the case.

> I don't really agree that it can be said to do a poor job without
> having any information about how the TWDA would look without "fear of
> contestation", but I see your point.

Yeah, see, the TWDA certainly can't indicate what would happen
differently if things were different. But it can indicate that Arika,
the most obvious and powerful vampire one can think of, is also the
one that shows up in the TWDA most often. By a significant margin.

> However, "fear of contestation" could be doing a great job, since
> without it Arika would possibly show up 100 times more than now. And
> since that information isn't shown in the TWDA, the conclusion that
> "fear of contesting" doesn't do anything can't really be drawn from
> looking at the TWDA.

This is true. But as Arika *already* shows up most often by a
considerable margin, one can either conclude that:

A) It is possible that she would show up even more if the contestation
rules were less harsh (which I believe is unlikely).

B) Harsh contestation as a method to dissuade use of the most powerful/
obvious vampires isn't particularly effective (which I believe is
likely).

But yes, it is a conclusion one has to draw from the evidence, rather
than something patently iron clad.

-Peter

Messages.Author: Mathieu Rivero
Messages.Body:
> I'm all in favor of "a bit" harsh. But the current rules are more than just a
> bit harsh.

I completely agree to that. (for crypt cards. Library cards contesting
is ok as far as i am concerned.)

Now, this is some other stupid thought :
I know hardestadt and Rafael de corazon's cartexts (and, in another
extent, Mary Ann Blaire's) were meant to increase diversity by
potentially weakening Alexandra and Arika. Well. The fact is, Rafael
and Hardestadt seem to be weak. I know only one deck who uses
Hardestadt, and only one with Rafael. The first is a fighting deck, in
which hardestadt becomes alastor. The second deck features a combo
with chain of command/daring the dawn+Possession, and this deck only
uses rafael because of the +2 bleed and obfuscate. Back to my point.
these two seem weaker than the others because of their lack of
cardtext. thus they aren't played. and thus they just keep company to
dust under people's bed. They don't weaken Arika and alexandra as
effectively as wanted.

This was a huge development to say something about contesting issue
fixing on a card-based solution. The cards will seem weak. They will
be a burden and jam a hand. However, I find it interesting to give an
alternative to contesting with cards : decks which would be prone to
be contested would have to manage a few slots (i.e. be a tiny bit less
efficient) to cram in those cards. But I know I'll never play such
cards because I won't get them at the moment I need them - like in the
early game. That's why I think this issue must be dealt with either
crypt cards (but honestly I don't believe in that) or by a rule change
or addition, like those who were proposed on this thread.

And, Mr. LSJ, one last more thing ; what do you think about the
solutions proposed above? Need any help players can carry out? Just
ask ;)
Thanks for designing this game and keep it as interesting as it is
now. :)
